A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support a reliable comparison, including matching retained material across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: v2 reports original steering and prompt-injection experiments, cross-model transfer results, neuron interventions, HellaSwag evaluation and feature-pair annotation analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these original empirical results and adds aggregate prompt-injection experiments, filtered steering results, Gemma-2-2B evaluation and shared-feature localization cases.

M1.justification: v3 supplements sampled-token prepending with a contiguous activation-text snippet procedure, including extending or truncating snippets and retaining the best intervention (Section 3.3, Appendix K.2). The underlying SAE-direction, token-gradient and neuron-steering mechanisms remain intact.

E1.justification: The generated next-token completion tasks, eight token-type categories and HellaSwag evaluation are retained. Added analyses reuse these task domains; Gemma-2-2B adds a model configuration, without introducing a new dataset or task.

E2.justification: The added aggregate prompt comparison uses features with interference 0.0–0.1 as its 'Random' reference instead of arbitrary random-token snippets (Appendix K.2). The original target, high-interference, low-interference and random-token comparators remain in Tables 1 and 5.

E3.justification: v3 adds an aggregate prompt protocol using optimized snippets and cosine/overlap scores alongside the retained top-30 success-rate evaluation. Appendix O introduces outcome-based screening of target features using thresholds around 0.05–0.1 and an additional Gemma-2-2B subsample experiment. These substantially extend the evaluation design.

E4.justification: New Appendix O investigates whether ineffective target features explain weak aggregate steering effects, and probes model-depth and metric explanations using Gemma-2-2B. Appendix K.2.1 additionally traces selected successful cases to three potential shared feature pairs and their layer locations. These add substantial diagnostic and case-study evidence.

E5.justification: v2's explicit statement of 100 injection-token samples per prompt disappears despite retention of the success-rate tables. Existing confidence-interval and significance-test conventions remain, while the added Gemma results in Figure 19 lack uncertainty intervals. These are reporting changes; fewer actual runs are not established.

E6.justification: v3 adds prompt response curves and regressions (Figures 5 and 15), filtered SAE results (Figure 18), Gemma-2-2B scores (Figure 19), and shared-pair localizations (Table 6). Original Tables 1 and 5 and the HellaSwag results remain unchanged. The reported filtering gains concern selected cases under a new protocol, rather than same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix D generalizes the stated SAE forward map from ReLU to an activation function accommodating ReLU and TopK. This is a limited revision of the mathematical description. Section 2.1's explicit cosine formulas otherwise restate existing definitions, and the steering and gradient derivations remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introductory contributions and conclusion retain the central claims about semantically unrelated interference, cross-model transfer, counterintuitive representational structure and asymmetric effects in highly polysemantic neurons. The additions do not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: v2 attributes weaker GPT-2-Small steering effects plausibly to depth; v3 argues that depth alone is insufficient and discusses ineffective cases and metric-dependent effects (Section 3.1, Appendix O). It also interprets prompt-injection effects as concentrated on target-associated tokens. The formal limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v3 specifies SAE activation-function choices, snippet formatting and tuning, filtering thresholds, and how potential feature locations are estimated. Conversely, the earlier large-model steering description specifying one feature's top five activation texts is omitted. Hardware, timing and code/data access statements are retained.

R1.justification: v3 adds Gorton and Lewis (2025), 'Adversarial examples are not bugs, they are superposition,' to the introduction and references. Appendix A and the broader positioning relative to prior research remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The methods exposition and prompt/transfer sections receive localized rewriting and expansion, with new appendix subsections integrated into the existing structure. Author ordering, affiliation formatting and the publication header also change. Most prose and the overall narrative organization are retained.

P2.justification: v3 substantially expands the visual evidence with prompt-injection Figures 5 and 15, filtered-steering and Gemma Figures 18–19, and shared-pair Table 6. Table 1 moves into the transfer section, Figure 1 receives a fuller caption, and several other captions are rewritten. Existing plots and tables are otherwise largely retained.

improvement.justification: v3 improves methodological clarity and adds useful prompt-injection and diagnostic evidence, replacing v2's speculative depth explanation with a more qualified interpretation. These gains are limited by outcome-based filtering, sparse Gemma experiment details and removal of the 100-samples-per-prompt disclosure. The central findings remain stable, making the overall improvement limited.
